cost_model_checks.detail: The runner uses os.wait4 per PID without Popen.poll, starts wall at process launch, and ends it only at reap. The measured wall therefore includes curve/setup, table construction, target generation, collection/query, linear solve, validation, receipt output, polling, scheduler delay, and child exit. The parent durability interval after reap is separately recorded and excluded.

Every child records per-PID wait4 user/system CPU and byte-unit ru_maxrss; aggregate RUSAGE_CHILDREN is not used. Every child also has positive Darwin proc_pid_rusage physical-footprint samples at a requested 50 ms cadence. The 8 GiB guard is cooperative and sampled, so it is not an OS hard cap and can miss a between-sample peak.

At this exact boundary the candidate median matched wall ratio is 0.8707707745177595 (-12.9229%) and CPU ratio is 0.8725261235273012 (-12.7474%), while per-PID wait4 max RSS is 1.7623146675302557 (+76.2315%) and sampled peak is 1.764409183488909 (+76.4409%) of baseline. The report preserves both speed and memory rather than presenting wall alone.

Offline locked build/test/toolchain wall, CPU, and RSS are preserved separately and were not amortized into per-target ratios, exactly as preregistered. The finite ratios therefore do not represent a deployment that rebuilds the executable for every target.
